author: vladimir_ea
content:
I have been running some simulations of seacast over gossip. Its only a small sim with few network hops. 16 validators, 1 attestation subnet with 3 aggregators.
 
- I initially did not see any reduction in bandwidth use for attestation aggregates and in fact it was somewhat worse with seacast than with plain gossip. 
- This was in contrast to execution payloads where seacast saved ~40% of bandwidth

The reason for the difference is due to the way aggregates are handled in gossip, When an aggregate is received, a node checks whether it already has an aggregate for the same committee that holds a superset of the votes in the new aggregate. If it does, it just ignores the new aggregate and does not forward it on gossip. This way duplicate aggregates are filtered out of the network - in my case aggregates and 2 and 3 were typically dropped. 

Seacast by contrast, was receiving and forwarding attestation chunks BEFORE the vote superset check (which only happens when chunks are decoded). So it was merrily forwarding the duplicate aggregates. 

- i added the attestor bitset to the seacast chunk metadata and deferred forwarding chunks of one aggregate if had already seen chunks for another superset aggregate
- bandwidth use for attestation aggregations is **reduced 50% vs gossip**
